fee_note: UNPAID lab pilot: $0 exchanged. The fee-as-demand-test is deliberately NOT exercised — the lab is not a customer and no purchase decision existed to test. A paid design-partner pilot remains the next step (see unsupported features).

data_boundary.secrets_scope: sentinel lab tokens only: work-scoped HMAC fixture secrets and fake-native bearer tokens against loopback services; no production credential exists anywhere in this pilot

unsupported_features: Paid model calls — the vendor is the controlled scripted vendor speaking the real codex app-server wire; token counts are real wire observations but no spend exists, so every cost metric is unknown by construction
A real design-partner customer — the named environment is the forge LAB, not a customer; no customer decided usefulness here and the decision owners are the maintainers

The live GitLab CE flow — refused by the #268 qualification (deployed control plane 0.28.0 vs the pinned v0.35.0 wheel; no budget caps; the GitLab dispatch seam carries no lane-resume contract); this pilot runs the offline production-entry seams instead

Cross-runner resume on the LIVE GitLab dispatch seam — the GitHub-lane parity gap recorded in qualification/profiles/gitlab-ce-v1.md section 8; exercised offline through the lane subprocess resume contract instead

Human review by partner engineers — acceptance is the lab operator's independent verification over seam artifacts (diffs, dispatch ledgers, checkpoint identities), never a model self-summary and never PR creation
The 4-8 week partner window — the lab window is its single execution day; the J-curve and adoption learning a real window buys do not exist here and are not claimed

ladder.scope: read-only over the fixture repositories; discovery questions and evidence-cited plans, no code changes land
ladder.authority: read-only; open questions answered by the lab operator through the durable answer surface

ladder.scope: single-area fixes inside lab/checkout verified by independent checks that do not trust the agent's self-report
ladder.authority: work happens in the fixture checkout's workspace generation; the operator collects and verifies the candidate

ladder.scope: multi-file changes inside lab/checkout whose decisive evidence cites the read-only neighbor lab/neighbor-contracts at exact OIDs
ladder.authority: collected candidate diffs; the operator accepts on seam evidence; the neighbor stays read-only

ladder.scope: the full failure, resume and intervention flows across runners on the lab seams (checkpoint authority, native dispatch ledger, control plane)
ladder.authority: ready_for_human gate: the operator decides on recorded seam artifacts before anything counts as delivered

criteria.statement: At least half the recorded tasks are accepted with zero human code change on the deliverable.
criteria.method: tracker fold over operator-recorded acceptance and human_code_change flags, judged at the named end date over all recorded tasks (blocked tasks included)

criteria.statement: At most half the recorded tasks carry an intervention event (partial steering counted exactly like a takeover).
criteria.method: tracker fold over recorded intervention events (steer/pause/resume/cancel/takeover/question_answer), judged at the named end date

criteria.statement: All-attempt spend per accepted task at or under $25 — expected UNJUDGEABLE at lab scope because no paid models run and spend is unknown, never zero.
criteria.method: tracker fold over the per-attempt usage ledger; any unrecorded spend keeps the criterion unjudgeable and named, never silently failed

dora.note: AUTHORED lab baseline, not a partner measurement: 30 minutes is the operator's planned manual time for one task of this shape (checkout, edit by hand, collect, verify by hand). No DORA four exist for the lab — there is no delivery pipeline history. cycle_time_vs_baseline is reported against this authored bound and never headlined.

review_cadence: after each task group completes — the lab pilot runs in one session, so the weekly operator cadence degenerates honestly to a per-group review pass
measurement_window_note: The window spans the spec freeze (2026-09-22, pre-kickoff) to the lab execution day (2026-09-23); criteria are judged at the named end date exactly as a partner pilot would judge them — but on lab-operational evidence only (see the provenance labels and the report's evidence class; the verdict bounds itself to the lab).
